question: How did the grant of Diwani rights of Bengal to the East India Company in 1765 fundamentally transform the pattern of bullion flow between Britain and India?
options: It increased the import of British bullion to build military infrastructure in Bengal.
It stopped the export of silver from Britain to India, as the Company used Bengal's land revenue surplus to purchase Indian goods for export.
It forced the Mughal Emperor to pay tribute in British gold coins.
It led to the complete demonetization of the silver rupee in Bengal.
explanation: Before 1765, the EIC had to import silver from Britain to buy Indian goods (export-import trade). After obtaining the Diwani (tax collection rights) of Bengal, they used the surplus territorial revenues to purchase ('invest' in) Indian textiles and other goods, thereby halting the flow of British bullion to India. This marks the beginning of the unilateral economic drain of wealth from India.
